I completely agree with your thoughtful approach here for several reasons:
Per-person numbers are much more relatable - when someone looks at these numbers, they can actually compare it to their own experience ("I spend about 20 hours a week on housework.

")
Moving away from "lazy partner" to terms like "primary domestic partner" or showing percentage splits (60/40, 70/30) is much more constructive and less judgmental.
It acknowledges the reality that perfectly equal splits are rare while avoiding blame.
Using percentage splits also allows people to self-identify where they fall on the spectrum.
Someone might look at it and think "Oh yes, I do about 70% of the housework" rather than having to categorize their partner as "lazy.

"

I'd suggest something like:
Single (100%)
Equal Partnership (50/50 split)
Primary/Secondary Partnership (70/30 split)

Or we could even show a range:
Single Person Household
Balanced Partnership (45-55% each)
Uneven Partnership (60-40% to 70-30% split)

This way people can recognize their situation without feeling defensive or criticized.
It's more about understanding patterns than making judgments.
